note: Payload families that are known not to be text, each derived from a named in-repo record and confirmed by a positive structural check. The filters read this file; an absent or unreadable inventory must fail closed rather than exclude nothing. Nothing enters this file on a signature alone.

check.detail: numProg is a u16 LE at +0x12; the header must be exactly 0x20 + 128*16 + numProg*16*32 + 512 bytes, which is the subfile's size

measured.basis: standalone (removed, removed_subfiles): measured with --no-windows --no-readable against --no-windows --no-payloads --no-readable, so the figure is what the exclusion accounts for on its own. marginal (removed_marginal): measured with the shape rule active, so it is what the exclusion still removes once unreadable runs are gone. Both are corpus-wide measurements made once and recorded here, because an excluded payload is never parsed at run time.

not_machine_identifiable.what: ct1 sprite packages (texel bands + CLUT + animation programs), ct3 finished VRAM pages, ct8 cue tables
not_machine_identifiable.why: the register names them by content type, but their payloads carry no documented signature and our tooling cannot derive the content type from the container's type-dependent load argument

not_machine_identifiable.what: object-mesh blocks and the mesh-group containers
not_machine_identifiable.why: the register states that the mesh block format belongs to the features/meshes chapter and names no payload signature for it

not_machine_identifiable.what: map geometry: tile and wall textures, corner heights, collision, visibility tables
not_machine_identifiable.why: described by structure and address, with no payload signature documented

signature_census.note: A census of every subfile's first four bytes finds only these two repeated ASCII-looking signatures; the other repeated heads are zero words, little-endian address words such as 0x320A8000, and similar non-signature content that no record names, so none of them is excluded.
